newsitem.title: UK: EBRD'S Quinn says more work needed to root reform.
newsitem.headline: EBRD'S Quinn says more work needed to root reform.

text.p: Former Soviet bloc countries have, despite some backsliding, made significant progress in the transition to market economies but more must be done to ensure reform takes root, EBRD President Ruairi Quinn said on Monday.

"There has been progress in spite of slippage and there have been significant achievements in democratisation, in privatisation and the attraction of both foreign direct and portfolio investment," Quinn said.
He was speaking at the opening of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's annual meeting in London.

"However, despite these reforms, significant improvements are still needed in many countries -- for example, corporate governance and micro-regulation must be improved if the reforms are to take root and if domestic savings and further foreign investment are to be attracted," he said.
Quinn said the countries also had to put in place the components of modern civic society, including the rule of law and efficient market regulation.
The EBRD was set up in 1991 to assist countries of eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union in their drive to transform themselves into modern market economies. It operates in 26 countries.
